candidates.evidence_text: Manchester's Co-op Live evacuated after 'unknown substance' let off in crowd at concert by US rapper Don Toliver - BBC News To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, Watch: Boos in the arena after concert cancelled as emergency services attend scene By Chris Graham Published 23 November 2026, 02:07 GMT Updated 3 hours ago Thousands of people were evacuated from a concert in Manchester on Sunday night after an "unknown substance" was released into the crowd, police said. The incident happened towards the end of US rapper Don Toliver's show at the Co-op Live arena at about 22:00. The North West Ambulance Service said one person was taken to hospital for further assessment while more than 50 people were assessed for "eye and respiratory symptoms". Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said a major incident was declared after reports of people suffering from the effects of an unknown substance, which police initially believed to be tear gas. Footage on social media showed emergency services converge on the arena, while some concertgoers were seen coughing as they streamed out of the venue. In a statement early on Monday, GMP said more than 12,000 people had been safely evacuated, with several people assessed for side effects. "Our priority was to ensure the safety of every person that was attending the concert," GMP Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said. "Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time. Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital. "We understand the concern that this incident will have raised – particularly those with loved ones at the venue last night – and we'd like to thank everyone for their patience as we dealt with it." Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Emergency services attended the Co-op Live arena in Manchester after a substance was let off in the crowd Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Concertgoers headed home after the performance was stopped by the incident She said the declaration of a major incident enabled the emergency services to coordinate a safe response. "We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about," she added. The ambulance service said: "Decontamination is being carried out as a precaution and one patient has been taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment. "We deployed several emergency crews, including our Hazardous Area Response Team, to support the safe assessment and treatment of people at the scene. "Anyone at tonight's event who has since noticed side-effects or become ill should seek medical advice." In a statement, Co-op Live said venue bosses were working closely with police to identify the cause of the incident. "Our priority remains the safety and security of all visitors to Co-op Live, and we will provide more information once we have an update from GMP," the statement said. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Don Toliver recently received five nominations for the 2027 Grammy awards (file photo) Toliver, whose real name is Caleb Zackery Toliver, was performing in Manchester as part of his Nitrous tour. The 32-year-old musician has received five nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards, including for Best New Artist. Get in touch Were you at the concert? candidates.evidence_text: ITV investigating Coronation Street actor Jacob Roberts after bar incident - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Jacob Roberts has starred in Coronation Street since 2024 By Miriam Barker North West Published 22 November 2026 ITV is investigating a Coronation Street actor following an alleged bar altercation. Jacob Roberts is known for playing Det Con Kit Green on the ITV soap since 2024. According to reports by the Sun newspaper, video footage appears to show him shouting outside Kiely's Irish Bar in Manchester on 8 November. Greater Manchester Police said officers had attended a bar in Watson Street at about 02:30 GMT following reports of a disturbance. No arrests have been made. An ITV spokesperson said they were investigating and would be speaking with Roberts. Roberts was allegedly trying to get into the bar, with staff claiming he was acting aggressively and swearing when he was told he could not come in as the venue was closing. Roberts previously played Damon Kinsella on the Channel 4 soap Hollyoaks from 2017 until 2023, before joining the cobbles in 2024. He has also appeared in Emmerdale and recently starred in the crossover episode Corridale. His storylines on Coronation Street include being diagnosed with male breast cancer as well as fathering a child after an illicit affair with his girlfriend's daughter. Roberts' representatives have been contacted for comment. candidates.summary: Jungle Junction nursery in Denton closed last month after a critical Ofsted inspection
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.

candidates.lead: Jungle Junction nursery in Denton closed last month after a critical Ofsted inspection
candidates.evidence_text: Parents shock at report of Denton nursery's safety failings - BBC News Image source, LDRS handout Image caption, Parents have told of their frustration at the nursery's sudden closure By George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 22 November 2026 Parents whose children went to a nursery that was shut down last month due to a "risk to children's safety" reacted as a report revealed the extent of inspectors' concerns. Jungle Junction in Denton, Greater Manchester, was temporarily closed in October by Ofsted and given a list of steps it needed to take in order to reopen. It included an order that "food is prepared in a way that prevents choking and children are within sight and hearing of staff". Denton Daycare Ltd later decided to permanently close, citing the company's "financial challenges". The watchdog report revealed inspectors also told the nursery to ensure proper hand washing routines were implemented, install better safeguarding procedures and give all children daily access to outdoor play. Arrangements for children with special educational needs and disabilities were also criticised. Denton Daycare Ltd company director Alina Naveed apologised to parents for the "difficult circumstances" they are facing having to find alternative childcare at such short notice - as well as staff. Keeley's three-year-old son was one of the nursery's children and she told the Local Democracy Reporting Service reading the Ofsted letter "left me feeling quite shocked" at the "sheer number and seriousness of the failures identified". "You expect [your child] to be safe, cared for and supported, and some of the things highlighted in that letter are really difficult to read," she added. Image source, LDRS handout Image caption, Jungle Junction nursery bosses decided to permanently close after its registration was suspended Other parents have described being hit financially by the sudden closure by having to pay extra nursery fees up front for replacement provision and fear they will not be compensated. Lauren had a four-year-old who went to the nursery and is one of many parents who claim to be left out of pocket after paying in advance for her son's care. She said: "If they were struggling financially, surely they would have pushed the prices up, then we would get the idea they were in financial difficulties." Naveed, who took over the nursery in January, said due to the financial position of the business, it will not be able to "meet all of these outstanding payments directly". She said: "I can only apologise sincerely to everyone affected and assure them that their concerns are being taken seriously." Jess, a former staff member who worked at Jungle Junction for six-and-a-half years, said new management took over in the summer and things went "downhill", with several issues becoming apparent. Naveed said: "When Ofsted suspended the nursery's registration, it placed an already struggling business in an extremely difficult position. "After considering the circumstances and whether reopening would be financially and operationally possible, I had to make the heartbreaking decision that the nursery could not continue." The names conjure images of a bespoke tailor’s business, an ornate label on an overcoat inside pocket The truth is much more sinister – those names spread fear across south Manchester’s Moss Side , they became bywords for the bullets, bloodshed and barbarity that blighted the deprived district in the 1990s. And the Gooch Close and Doddington crime gangs – locked in an unrelenting Claims surfaced that the 14-year-old died because he was mistaken for a Doddington member. He was not the only alleged victim of that terrifying feud – the catalogue of casualties is hard to comprehend Carl Stapleton, just 17, was fatally attacked with a machete on Alexandra Park estate in April, 1991, suffering 15 wounds. His crime? Being friendly with members of the Gooch mob In the same year, 21-year-old Darren Samuels was added to the list after being shot dead. A trial of two suspects was scrubbed after an eyewitness refused to give evidence. Julian Stewart, also 21 and described as a prominent Doddington member, was shot in the head in January, 19

Emergency services and police attended the scene and a cordon was put in place outside the venue.. Police asked people to stay away from the arena while emergency services managed the evacuation and helped concertgoers get to transport home.. In a statement, Co-op Live said it will work with police to identify what happened and 'appropriate action' to be taken.. Emergency services have also told anyone who was at the gig to seek medical attention if they feel unwell in the next few days.. A major incident has been declared by police. . . . . . . Add to preferred sources . . Comments . . News . Charlotte Fisher Reporter . . 00:07, 23 Nov 2026 Updated 06:18, 23 Nov 2026 . . . . . . Scene inside Co-op live during Don Toliver gig . . . . Concertgoers at Co-op Live in Manchester were evacuated on Sunday night (November 22), during Don Toliver’s NITROUS show. Emergency services and police attended the scene and a cordon was put in place outside the venue.. Eyewitnesses said the standing area was cleared at around 10pm, shortly after Don Toliver finished performing on the B stage.. Greater Manchester Police said an 'unknown substance' - reported to be tear gas - was released into the crowd towards the end of the concert.. Over 12,000 fans in attendance were evacuated immediately.. A major incident was declared by police, with one fan in hospital.. Over 50 people fell ill and were medically assessed, paramedics said.. A video that captured the moment officials formally stopped the event shows a staff member telling the audience the show was finished and asked people to leave via the nearest exit.. GMP said those showing signs of being affected were being supported by emergency services. Police added that no serious injuries had been reported but one person was in hospital.. Police asked people to stay away from the arena while emergency services managed the evacuation and helped concertgoers get to transport home.. In a statement, Co-op Live said it will work with police to identify what happened and 'appropriate action' to be taken.. Emergency services have also told anyone who was at the gig to seek medical attention if they feel unwell in the next few days.. No arrests have been at this stage, and nor have any serious injuries been reported.. READ THE FULL STORY: LIVE: Co-op Live evacuated and police descend on venue . . Follow men: Facebook . X (Twitter) . Instagram . Comments . . . . ‌ . . ‌ . . . . ‌ . . ‌

candidates.evidence_text: Charity 'I'm a children's nurse, but seeing my premature baby in an incubator terrified me' Staff at Wythenshawe Hospital are hoping to bring a little Christmas magic to poorly children Jensen was born premature at Wythenshawe Hospital (Image: MFT) Add to preferred sources Comments News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 18:33, 22 Nov 2026 A mum whose baby boy was born prematurely at just 33 weeks is determined to help make Christmas special for other poorly children after experiencing life on the other side of hospit Lauren Mulhern, a children's nurse at Royal Manchester Children's Hospital, knows only too well how important the little things can be for families spending the festive season in hospital after her son Jensen spent three weeks receiving specialist neonatal care following his birt Jensen was transferred to the Local Neonatal Unit at Wythenshawe Hospital immediately after his birth in May 2025, where he spent three weeks receiving specialist support with his breathing and feeding before he was finally able to go home Now, grateful for the care her family received, Lauren has completed her first half marathon, raising £500 for the neonatal unit, and hopes to take on the Manchester Marathon next year to help other families facing similar experiences Lauren, who has worked as a children's nurse at Royal Manchester Children's Hospital since qualifying in 2017, said her pregnancy had been far from straightforward, with concerns meaning she and her husband were aware Jensen would probably arrive early

They want to replace the 766 flats, most of which sit empty, with 601 new homes The scheme would provide a mix of flats and townhouses - with a shift towards more family homes from a setup of mainly bedsits and one-beds The Seven Sisters - actually named College Bank - have become part of the furniture. Lots of Rochdalians having either lived there, or had friends and family live there To imagine travelling down the M62 and not seeing the brutalist siblings protruding into the sky seems odd. But it only takes one trip around the estate to realise the blocks have gotten into a sorry state

candidates.evidence_text: Co-Op Live . Need to know. Don Toliver 'tear gas' incident at Co-op Live as 12,000 fans evacuated with one in hospital - all we know so far. A major incident has been declared by police. . . . . . . Add to preferred sources . . Comments . . News . Charlotte Fisher Reporter . . 00:07, 23 Nov 2026 Updated 06:18, 23 Nov 2026 . . . . . . Scene inside Co-op live during Don Toliver gig . . . . Concertgoers at Co-op Live in Manchester were evacuated on Sunday night (November 22), during Don Toliver’s NITROUS show. Emergency services and police attended the scene and a cordon was put in place outside the venue.. Eyewitnesses said the standing area was cleared at around 10pm, shortly after Don Toliver finished performing on the B stage.. Greater Manchester Police said an 'unknown substance' - reported to be tear gas - was released into the crowd towards the end of the concert.. Over 12,000 fans in attendance were evacuated immediately.. A major incident was declared by police, with one fan in hospital.. Over 50 people fell ill and were medically assessed, paramedics said.. A video that captured the moment officials formally stopped the event shows a staff member telling the audience the show was finished and asked people to leave via the nearest exit.. GMP said those showing signs of being affected were being supported by emergency services. Police added that no serious injuries had been reported but one person was in hospital.. Police asked people to stay away from the arena while emergency services managed the evacuation and helped concertgoers get to transport home.. In a statement, Co-op Live said it will work with police to identify what happened and 'appropriate action' to be taken.. Emergency services have also told anyone who was at the gig to seek medical attention if they feel unwell in the next few days.. No arrests have been at this stage, and nor have any serious injuries been reported.. READ THE FULL STORY: LIVE: Co-op Live evacuated and police descend on venue . . Follow men: Facebook . candidates.evidence_text: Charity 'I'm a children's nurse, but seeing my premature baby in an incubator terrified me' Staff at Wythenshawe Hospital are hoping to bring a little Christmas magic to poorly children Jensen was born premature at Wythenshawe Hospital (Image: MFT) Add to preferred sources Comments News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 18:33, 22 Nov 2026 A mum whose baby boy was born prematurely at just 33 weeks is determined to help make Christmas special for other poorly children after experiencing life on the other side of hospit Lauren Mulhern, a children's nurse at Royal Manchester Children's Hospital, knows only too well how important the little things can be for families spending the festive season in hospital after her son Jensen spent three weeks receiving specialist neonatal care following his birt Jensen was transferred to the Local Neonatal Unit at Wythenshawe Hospital immediately after his birth in May 2025, where he spent three weeks receiving specialist support with his breathing and feeding before he was finally able to go home Now, grateful for the care her family received, Lauren has completed her first half marathon, raising £500 for the neonatal unit, and hopes to take on the Manchester Marathon next year to help other families facing similar experiences Lauren, who has worked as a children's nurse at Royal Manchester Children's Hospital since qualifying in 2017, said her pregnancy had been far from straightforward, with concerns meaning she and her husband were aware Jensen would probably arrive early

However under local government transparency rules introduced in 2015, councils across the country who use them are required to publish what payments have been made to reassure pe Oldham council have now admitted they have not been revealing how these cards were being used and what taxpayer money has been spent on for eleven years. This is after no public records for payments were found by the Manchester Evening News The council is now working on publishing seven years' worth of payment records, which is understood to be the length of time this data is required to be kept. Over this period, over £1m was spent by council and school staff

candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 10:33am Kirith Entwistle, the Labour MP for Bolton North East, has said she found the current court system "triggering" and had to watch her abuser "stare at her". Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Altrincham-based Urbanize originally proposed a 22-storey building on the plot but subsequently reduced its height to 13 storeys The proposals did not materialise, and the council took control of the site in 2019 Under early-stage plans being developed by Westshield and MSV, around 110 social rent homes could be delivered on the site

candidates.evidence_text: The infant, named Ava by Greater Manchester Police, was discovered by a dog walker near Ashtons Field, in Little Hulton, Salford, on 20 November 2024 Despite a long-running investigation and a £50,000 reward put up by the Greater Manchester combined authority, detectives have still not been able to identify the child's mother Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said its determination to find the answers "has never wavered", and that it wanted to "secure the justice that Ava deserves" Det Insp Louise Kelly said: "We know 20 November will be particularly significant for Ava's parents, family members, and anyone who may have known her." She added: "Behind every line of enquiry, every review of evidence, and every piece of information we assess is a baby girl who will never be forgotten." Kelly said the force was currently trying to organise a funeral for Ava

candidates.lead: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund
candidates.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

candidates.evidence_text: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat The challenge, delivered by The Reading Agency in partnership with public libraries, encouraged children to discover the joy of reading through the theme Read to the Beat, celebrating music, rhythm and the power of stories Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton’s providing new forms of support for residents struggling with the cost of living, as presented at Bolton’s Tackling Poverty networking event held at Bolton Albert Halls on November 12 The cost of living is a major concern for many, and it may get tougher during the winter, as such, the event and the targeted support offered to people across Bolton offer some reassurance to those worst affected The support spans a large number of areas including helping access emergency food, heating, and financial assistance The event brings those organisations providing support together so they can better understand what is available across the town and as such can make informed decisions about who to refer people to for the most appropriate help In total there were over 40 organisations attending the event including the public, voluntary, and community sector, and other parters who were highlighting their services all were encouraged to network, share information, and create a more connected and efficient framework The presentations highlighted how Bolton’s Tacking Poverty Strategy can make a real difference, and how the Crisis, and Resilience Fund is being allocated to help groups across the borough

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Venue The Warehouse, Aviva Studios, Water Street, Manchester, M3 4JQ . . History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.lead: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre […] The post Sona Jobarteh Tour appeared first on Band on the Wall
candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo translates to matchstick and is a nod to Manchester-based painter LS Lowry’s ‘matchstick men’ style.. . Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. Local groups looking for a friendly, flexible venue will be encouraged to get in touch.. . Vix Connolly, General Manager, Fosforo Lounge said: “We’re so looking forward to welcoming everyone to Fosforo Lounge on the 28th November. The group’s approach centres on cooking over fire, carefully-sourced ingredients, expertly-pr Sam Elliott, Chef-Owner of Pasture, commented: “Manchester is a city with a huge personality, a strong independent spirit and a real passion for great food, so bringing Pasture here is incredibly exciting. St Michael’s gives us the opportunity to create something that goes beyond “From our signature open-fire cooking at Pasture Manchester and Mediterranean-inspired all-day dining at Terrace, to the atmosphere of W Lounge and the much-loved character of the Abercromby, we’re looking forward to becoming part of the city’s dynamic hospitality scene.”

Vast in scale, the production features a huge cast of voca The show provides Phelim McDermott, acclaimed director and co-founder of Improbable, with the opportunity to complete the Glass Portrait Trilogy . Having directed Satyagraha in 2026 and the Grammy and Olivier Award-winning production of Akhnaten in 2016 for English National Opera The star-studded lineup also sees the BBC Philharmonic Orchestra, led by acclaimed conductor and composer Brad Lubman, return to the venue following their collaboration with ENO and Factory International on the genre-defying opera, Angel’s Bone . Meanwhile, a 16-strong vocal ense Einstein on the Beach will run in Philip Glass’s 90th year, opening at Aviva Studios from Sat 29 May 2027 – Sat 12 June 2027, followed by its North American premiere at the Park Avenue Armory, New York

Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

In August, Nothing Gold Can Stay took Robert Frost’s poem about transience as its starting point. Where that show dwelt on things passing, this one is more interested in what lasts The four contributing artists each approach time differently, thinking about how the past and the future shape the way ideas are understood. Anna Clough, a Cumbrian-born artist based at Salford’s Paradise Works, has made walking performances tracing mining landscapes from the Neo Sheffield’s Charlotte Dawson treats everyday objects – souvenirs, collections – as vessels for memory. Olivia England, who graduated from Manchester School of Art alongside Clough, reworks found objects, text and imagery through bookbinding and print, while London-based Elliot Fo Seeing the work from a perspective that isn’t your own is meant to open up conversations about the legacy of ideas, collective memory and what our actions leave behind for people we’ll never meet

evidence_packet.evidence_text: @ Sticks'n'Sushi Manchester on Every Saturday Settle in for an All You Can Sip Brunch at none other than Manchester's Japanese-Scandinavian restaurant, Sticks'n'Sushi. Up to their usual tasty tricks, this spot is serving a DJ-led Saturday brunch that will have you munching everything from karaage chicken to spicy tuna maki rolls and seaweed salad. They'll start by bringing out a bunch of sharing plates for the table, before each guest is permitted to pick 3 dishes from the maki, nigiri and sticks portion of the menu. A mango coconut rice pudding will serve as the perfect refresher, and you may still have some drinks to get through by the end of the meal – as they'll be free-flowing for 90 minutes. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Altrincham Market and market house, part restaurant, part market, part town square. Food, drink, shopping and more Altrincham ‪Market House. Eat, meet, drink, shop, watch, talk, listen, laugh. Come in, be yourself and if you like it bring your friends! Altrincham’s charter dates back to 1290, it’s location at the intersection of the Cheshire farm belt and the commercial commuter zone of Manchester means the town has a long and important history. Altrincham market is now at the heart of the regeneration of ‘the modern market tow The covered market hosts regional food producers, vintage fashion and furniture, home & garden and contemporary craft on a Tuesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday Altrincham Market House Opening Hours Tues-Sat : 9am-10pm Sun : 9am-6pm Mon : Closed The Outdoor Market (Shopping) Tues: 8am-3pm Fri: 8am-3pm Sat: 8am-4pm Sun: 10am-4pm Altrincham Market House is home to award-winning independent quality food operators. These include the following: Honest Crust – wood fired pizza “among the country’s best”. Tender Cow who serve rare breed flat iron steak and chips. Jack in the Box selling fantastic craft beers. candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC What Mauricio Pochettino said he'd learnt about his Man United players in Liverpool nightmare Mauricio Pochettino saw his Man Utd reign get off to a horror start with a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield. Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United need to "accept the reality" that they are in a relegation battle, but said he saw plenty of positives in the heavy defeat to Liverpool that got his reign off to a horror start United had Leny Yoro sent off just eight minutes into Pochettino's first game in charge, and Liverpool ran riot after that, scoring four times and missing many more chances as they piled up 28 shots It keeps Pochettino's side in 19th in the Premier League table and they have just eight points from 11 games, while their winless run in the league will stretch to three months by the time they face Brentford next weekend Despite the nature of the defeat and the fact United conceded four for the third time in their last six games, Pochettino saw enough fight and desire in his players to believe they can drag themselves out of trouble Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News!
